title: 🔥 The Roast: Week 6
preview: Brad took the biggest beating of the season, Maddox's Unbreakable Vow got re-bound, the Commish let three running backs rot on his bench, and overtime murdered the median. Tap if you can take it.
schedule_note: New roasts drop every Wednesday at 6 PM ET, right after waivers and before Thursday night.
intro: Wow, that just happened. What's next? Week 5 gave us a 70.7-point blowout, three overtime games that wrecked the median, and a commissioner who benched fifty points of running backs. Week 6 kicks off Thursday. Nobody is safe.
facts_note: Every fact is real Sleeper data: Week 5 results and lineups, transactions through Wednesday Oct 14 at 5 PM ET (including the overnight waiver run and the day's free-agent and commissioner moves), injuries, and Week 6 matchups. "Projected" = Sleeper Week 6 projections in league scoring for lineups as set Wednesday around 5:30 PM ET (lineups can change). A roast among friends.

entries.roast: Ryan lost to Taylor by 4.75 and had FIFTY points of running back sitting on his own bench: Braelon Allen 20.6, Blake Corum 16.2, Emanuel Wilson 13.2. Any one of them wins the game. Instead Jeremiyah Love started and scored 2.2, which is what you get when you let a man who wrote the rulebook also write the lineup. Braelon, you let the whole team down. Blake, you let the whole team down. Emanuel, you let the whole team down. Nobody let anybody down, Commish, you're the only one in the building with a pencil. Bo Nix gave him 6.65 and the Steelers defense gave him 1.5, so he started the two worst-looking guys on the board and benched the three who could've saved him. Supreme Leader, my ass. Supreme Leader of the bench.
entries.this_week: vs Kyle Llano. Projected 151.6 to 145.6. Braelon Allen (11.4) is on the bench again, behind Jeremiyah Love (10.1).
entries.prediction: Ryan wins by 6, and Braelon Allen scores 15 on the bench, because of course he does.

entries.roast: Brad lost by 70.7, the biggest blowout of the season, and he did it with two quarterbacks scoring 61.8 points. Josh Allen 35.1, Brissett 26.7, and the rest of the team was out getting a sandwich. RJ Harvey gave him 0.7. Kamara 2.6. CeeDee Lamb 2.9. Waddle 4.8. That's four skill players for 11 points total, my man, I've seen better production from a group chat. Emeka Egbuka dropped 17.2 on his bench, because of course. He conceded before the game was even over, which makes it the only thing Brad finished early all year. 941.5 points against through five weeks, and the sweetheart of the league has the defense of a screen door in a hurricane. Everybody loves Brad. Nobody loves Brad's secondary.
entries.this_week: vs Mike Hemstreet. Projected 144.0 to 133.1. Mahomes is back next to Josh Allen, and the new kicker (Nick Folk, off waivers) and new defense (Chiefs, added at 6:01 this morning) cover the Detroit and Cincinnati byes.
entries.prediction: Brad wins by 11 and still gives up 130, which for him counts as a rest day.

entries.roast: Maddox put up 218.2, high score of the week, with Gibbs for 41.7 and Bucky Irving for 35.0, and he STILL left 100.9 points on his bench, including Matthew Golden's 22.8 and Malik Willis's 16.75. That's some guy winning the lottery and framing the ticket. He started Colston Loveland for 3.9, because even the guy who wins by 70 has to leave a little room to be a dumbass. Then there's Shedeur Sanders. Maddox cut that man like a bad tattoo, and the Commish keeps sewing him back on. In Harry Potter, you break one and you die. In this league, you break one and it just keeps showing up on your roster. And I think that's worse. This week he's starting a Vikings defense that's on bye. The man is a genius with a clipboard and a fool with a calendar.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Cardillo. Projected 124.0 to 111.0. Maddox is starting the Vikings defense, the same Vikings D he offered up in the Shedeur ransom, and Minnesota is on bye. That's a zero in the lineup until he fixes it. Bucky Irving is questionable, and Shedeur is on the bench, where the vow can keep an eye on him.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins anyway, cuts Shedeur by Friday, and Shedeur is back by Saturday.

entries.roast: Brian is 7-3, second in the league, and his kicker Cairo Santos scored ZERO. Not low. Zero. A kicker with a zero is a guy who got paid to show up to the meeting and went to the bathroom. Deshaun Watson gave him 6.75 at superflex, Dalton Kincaid 3.7, Rome Odunze 4.0, and Jacory Croskey-Merritt dropped 14.2 on the bench because Brian takes his lineup advice from a Magic 8-Ball. Jaylen Warren put up 39.8 and carried the whole damn operation on his back while Brian sat there like he had a plan. There's a silhouette on a rooftop tonight, a masked figure in the dark, and I'm told he's 7-3 and has no idea how. Somebody flip the signal. He's still asleep.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Kasik. Projected 142.8 to 151.6. Bryce Young starts with Deshaun Watson at superflex, and Caleb Williams (doubtful) stays on the bench.
entries.prediction: Brian loses by 8 and nobody hears about it until Tuesday.

entries.roast: Kasik lost to Mike by 4.0, and anybody can see why, because the evidence was sitting right there on his bench. Justin Herbert started at superflex for 6.95 while Daniel Jones sat there with 13.75. Jameson Williams scored 18.7 on the bench. J.K. Dobbins scored 15.4 on the bench. The Seahawks defense scored 11.3 on the bench while the Jaguars started for 5.0. That's 59.15 points sitting on the bench, 15 times the margin he lost by. What's the deal with lawyers? They bill you for every hour and never once look at the thing you hired them to look at. Matt Gay gave him 5.0. I've seen a guy at a bachelor party kick better. Objection, Nick. Sustained.
entries.this_week: vs Brian Mulvihill. Projected 151.6 to 142.8. Zay Flowers and Nico Collins are both questionable starters, and Daniel Jones finally starts at QB next to Herbert.
entries.prediction: Kasik wins by 9 and bills Brian for the hours.

entries.roast: Mike survived a Sunday night overtime against Kasik, beat him by 4, and still found a way to lose. Look at his lineup. DK Metcalf started for 4.3, Chase Brown for 6.0, and Ollie Gordon sat there with 14.8. Travis Kelce got a 0.0 on a bye week, which, honestly, is the most efficient thing about this roster. And T.J. Hockenson, the same Hockenson he benched for a 26.9 the week before, finally got his start and gave him 1.7. Mike and Hockenson break up more than a reality TV couple, and Mike always takes him back, and he's always the one who gets robbed. He's 6-4 and a cop. Watch out. He'll arrest a guy, drop him, pick him back up on waivers, and arrest him again. That's not law enforcement, brother, that's catch and release.
entries.this_week: vs Brad Kochheiser. Projected 133.1 to 144.0. Lamar Jackson (questionable, 21.4 projected) sits for Jameis Winston (13.1), Kelce is back at tight end with Hockenson on bye, and Mike Evans and DeVonta Smith are questionable starters.
entries.prediction: Mike loses by 7, and Lamar's points on the bench get entered into evidence.

entries.roast: Kyle lost by 8.15 and scored the lowest total of the week at 129.6, and you want to know the sad part? He had it on his bench. D'Andre Swift gave him 17.3 sitting there. Germie Bernard gave him 14.4 on the bench. Tucker Kraft, 12.1. Kyle started Romeo Doubs for 2.6. Tee Higgins for 4.2. Swap Swift in for Doubs and he wins by six, and his whole bench put up 82.8 while he was out looking for a loophole. And what's a fumble worth in this league? One point. He needed NINE reversed fumbles to win. Nine. That's not a challenge flag, that's a class action. Fumble not lost. You don't get partial credit for dropping the ball in front of the crowd, Kyle. Ask any guy who dropped the cake at a wedding and wanted partial credit for the frosting.
entries.this_week: vs Ryan Nussdorfer. Projected 145.6 to 151.6. Goff and St. Brown are on the Lions' bye, so Stafford and Sam Darnold run the quarterback spots.
entries.prediction: Kyle loses by 6 and files a formal complaint about the fumble rule. Denied.

entries.roast: Drew won 212.55 to 145.45 and the man did it with a 'team got healthy' shrug. Puka Nacua dropped 39.7. Isaiah Likely 32.4. Jayden Daniels 33.75, Sam LaPorta 19.8, and the Packers defense added 23.05 for a man whose quarterback is Kirk Cousins at 13.65. And Daniels and LaPorta are the same two he tried to trade to Cardillo this week, then started against him, and they put 53.55 on him. You tried to sell the guy the gun, and then you shot him with it! That's cold. That's Pat Fitzgerald flipping off the Illinois sideline cold, and you know what? I'd follow that man into a war. Drew's version of war is a text that says 'watch out' with a smirk emoji. Four-and-six and acting like he's undefeated. Watch out, folks. Watch out.
entries.this_week: vs Taylor Alvarado. Projected 138.8 to 136.6. Jayden Daniels, Puka Nacua and Jalen Coker are all questionable in the starting lineup, with Geno Smith (13.6) waiting on the bench.
entries.prediction: Drew wins by 3 and posts "watch out" again, unprompted.

entries.roast: Taylor beat the Commish by 4.75, and it was a tremendous win, maybe the best win, people are saying it. Christian Watson put up 35.3. Aaron Rodgers 24.35. Spencer Shrader, the KICKER, 21.0, and Taylor will tell you he hoards kickers for strategy. Meanwhile Cam Skattebo gave him 6.1, Michael Wilson 7.35 and the Commanders defense 5.1, and somebody needs to check Taylor's lineup for a pulse. Now he's got Colts D, defense number eight since August. Eight! The Pentagon changes less hardware. And his tight end room is Tyler Higbee, Kyle Pitts, Dallas Goedert, Darren Waller. He didn't build a roster, he built a Tight End Convention, and the keynote is Goedert, who's doubtful. Sad! Very, very sad!
entries.this_week: vs Drew Hartman. Projected 136.6 to 138.8. Dallas Goedert (doubtful) is the starting tight end while Kyle Pitts, Darren Waller and Tyler Higbee sit, and the brand-new Colts defense gets its first start.
entries.prediction: Taylor loses by 2, blames the defense, and defense number nine shows up by Friday.

entries.roast: Cardillo scored 145.45 and lost by 67.1. Drake Maye went off for 45.2, the highest single score in the league. George Pickens added 30.0. Trevor Lawrence added 23.55, the Texans defense added 19.7, and still the man was nearly 70 points down. Because Jaylen Wright gave him 1.1, Carnell Tate 1.6, Harold Fannin 1.4, and Roschon Johnson, 9.0, made it the entire running game. Listen to me, Nick. I've seen better rosters at a Costco free sample table. Michael Penix put up 14.3 on the bench. And the median beat him by 1.18 when three games went to overtime and not one of his players was in them. Rookie mistake. Next year, draft guys who play in overtime.
entries.this_week: vs Jacob Maddox. Projected 111.0 to 124.0, the lowest set lineup in the league. Carnell Tate (14.0) sits behind Luther Burden (12.3) at flex, the running backs are Kyle Monangai (4.6) and Roschon Johnson (4.3), and Maddox is starting a Vikings defense that's on bye.
entries.prediction: Cardillo loses by 9, and every game in the league goes to overtime except his.
